items.title: Joe Williams interviewed by Leslie Gourse, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: Monk Rowe also participated briefly in the interview.

ctx.x: He has been a professional jazz singer since 1937 and had worked with Coleman Hawkins, Lionel Hampton, Andy Kirk and Red Saunders before joining the Count Basie band in 1954. His contribution to that ensemble “elevated the entire band to a new plateau of commercial success,” according to jazz critic Leonard Feather. Since becoming a solo singer in 1961, he has been equally successful at a time when rock threatened to swamp the world of jazz music. His recording output has never dwindled through the 60s, 70s, and…
Joe was interviewed by his biographer, Leslie Gourse, on March 9, 1996 in New York City. Monk Rowe also participated briefly in the interview.
We are filming for the Hamilton College Archives. This is Joe Williams and I’m Leslie Gourse. I need the introduction, Joe does not.
